site.name: Livingston Mine
site.location: Sugarloaf Mountain / Sugar Loaf Mining District
overview: The Livingston Mine was one of the principal gold producers of Boulder County's Sugar Loaf Mining District on Sugarloaf Mountain.

Period federal mineral reporting describes the mine as developed by shafts and identifies it among the county's important producers, while surviving 1890s photographs document its mine buildings and workers.

timeline.text: Historic preservation research identifies the Livingston as one of the Sugar Loaf district's principal producers during this period.
A surviving Boulder Historical Society photograph documents the Livingston Mine on Sugarloaf Mountain, including mine buildings and miners.
U.S. Geological Survey mineral reporting described the Livingston as a shaft-developed mine and one of Boulder County's important producers.

moreHistory: History Colorado preservation documentation uses the Livingston as an example of Boulder County's modestly successful shaft operations and identifies a shaft house containing hoisting and boiler equipment with a headframe beneath the peak of the structure.

The Carnegie Library for Local History preserves multiple photographs specifically identified as the Livingston Mine on Sugarloaf Mountain, including a dated 1893-1894 view and additional views dating broadly from 1885-1910.

The mapped mine-level identification point at approximately 40.0258195, -105.4130504 is used as the location anchor. Remnant does not claim that this coordinate is a field-surveyed surviving shaft collar.
